request.spec:
Show a due-total per calendar month: for every month (yyyy-mm) that any claim on the sheet is
dated in, the due of the claims dated in that month that count.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show a due-total per calendar month: for every month (yyyy-mm) that any claim on the sheet is
dated in, the due of the claims dated in that month that count.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now shows a due-total for each calendar month, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

The new "Months" table sits just below the existing "Tags" table and is built the same way. It's a new `MonthTotals` component in `src/main/frontend/features/rates/rates.slot.tsx`:

- **Which months appear:** every yyyy-mm that any claim on the sheet is dated in, whatever its status. So a month that holds only draft or voided claims still gets a row, showing `0.00`. Months are listed oldest first.
- **What each total adds up:** the due of that month's claims that count, using the same rule as the existing rollup totals. Settled claims count. Open and pending claims count unless the person was on hold for that date and the claim isn't on a statement. Deferred claims don't count, and a due shown as n/a counts as 0.
- **Test anchor:** each total carries `data-testid="month-<yyyy-mm>-due-total"`, matching the spec.

This was a front-end change only. Every figure needed is already in the claim, rate and hold data the screen loads, so nothing changed in the stored data, the server or the audit file.
